revision.supersedes: Company-displacement framing and churn-first timing gate
revision.unit: Belief revision about replicable software rents
revision.hypothesis: Technically informed builders may see collapsing replication and migration costs before investors adjust the durability and terminal value of software subscriptions. ArtCraft is a demonstrator, not the required winner.

decision: Promote this from a company watch to an active software-rent repricing thesis. Do not require reported churn before considering a narrative-driven valuation reset. An Adobe short still needs evidence of incremental surprise versus existing AI pessimism, a credible diffusion catalyst, valuation sensitivity and executable risk/borrow economics. Those are not yet established by this curated public sample.

gates.name: Incremental technical surprise
gates.next: Validate replication cost, breadth and familiar-workflow preservation relative to prior AI expectations; ArtCraft revenue not required.

gates.name: Expectation gap and valuation
gates.next: Compare current implied durability and multiples with a range of rent erosion; broad AI fear is already public.

gates.name: Diffusion catalyst and timing
gates.next: Look for independent replication, credible creator trials and dated financial coverage; maintain first-observed timestamps without asserting first-ever.

gates.name: Market confirmation and confounds
gates.next: Compare ADBE with IGV and QQQ; inspect peers, volume, residual paths and co-occurring events. No price move is not proof of ignorance.

gates.name: Borrow and risk budget
gates.next: Obtain actual borrow/recall terms and define loss budget/horizon; correct technological direction does not guarantee short P&L.

claims.text: ArtCraft can be an informative replication demonstration even if its company and current alpha products fail commercially.
claims.falsifier: Independent builds show most apparent depth is superficial or the method cannot replicate beyond a demo.

claims.text: Replicating familiar interaction patterns could erode learned-usage lock-in; file, team and ecosystem switching costs remain separate hypotheses.
claims.falsifier: Task completion and migration remain costly despite an apparently familiar interface.

claims.text: Markets can compress expected software rents before observed customer churn; churn is a later fundamental test, not a necessary trigger.
claims.falsifier: New technical validation does not change expectations after sector controls, or pricing already discounts the outcome.

claims.text: The broad AI application-layer disruption thesis reached financial reporting before ArtCraft. A completely hidden sector-wide story is untenable.
claims.falsifier: This does not resolve how much additional replication risk Adobe prices today.

claims.text: DeepSeek contested proprietary model economics directly; Nvidia is an observable listed proxy for a transmitted capex/compute narrative, not a direct OpenAI or Anthropic equity return.
claims.falsifier: Do not identify model-vendor competitive losses with supplier stock losses.

claims.text: The declared October Adobe price window does not demonstrate an ArtCraft selloff or a measured information advantage.
claims.falsifier: Longer matched tape and timestamped expectations could reveal an effect not isolated by daily returns.
